info.album: I Never Loved a Man the Way I Love You

podcast.body: Aretha Franklin's iconic cover version of Otis Redding's song, which topped the Hot 100 on June 3rd, 1967. This rendition is celebrated as a feminist anthem and was named the greatest single of all time by Rolling Stone magazine. "Aretha Franklin's cover of Respect topped the Hot 100."

srcs.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia
Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia

podcast.body: Originally written and recorded by Otis Redding in 1965, Franklin's cover is widely considered the greatest pop cover of all time due to its transformative power. She flipped the gender, added new sections like the R-E-S-P-E-C-T spelling and the "Socket To Me" chant, and remade it into a feminist anthem about a woman demanding her own money and proper deference. Released as the second single from her Atlantic debut album in April 1967, it climbed to number one on both the Hot 100 and the R&B chart by June. "Just by singing about earning her own money and demanding her proper from her man, Franklin remade respect into a feminist anthem and a chart topping smash."

podcast.body: This iconic song was Franklin's last number one pop chart hit before "I Knew You Were Waiting (For Me)" in 1987, almost exactly 20 years later. "Almost exactly 20 years after Franklin had last topped the big pop chart with respect."
